title.narrative: VOSIEDA Climate Smart Agriculture for Resilience and Livelihood Support
VOSIEDA Climate Smart Agriculture for Resilience and Livelihood Support

description.narrative: Insatsen kommer att bidra till att minska klimatförändringarnas påverkan för de mest utsatta människorna, av vilka majoriteten är kvinnor som lever i fattigdom. Aktiviteterna är inriktade på att stötta småskaliga jordbrukare att anpassa och utveckla sina jordbruksmetoder, inklusive att främja användningen av organiska gödningsmedel framför kemiska, att förflytta sig från svedjebruk och på så sätt bidra till skydd av skog och bevarandet av viktiga kolsänkor

The initiative will contribute to reducing the impact of climate change on the most vulnerable people, majority of whom are women living in poverty. Activities are targeted at helping smallholder farmers adjust and improve their farming practices, including promoting the use of organic fertilizers over chemical fertilizers, moving away from shifting cultivation, thus, contributing to protection of forest, and preserving important carbon sinks.

title.narrative: Grant Agreement between Sida and VOSIEDA

description.narrative:
Year Two focused on ramping up project activities in alignment with the approved work plan and budget. Below are the key achievements reported by VOSIEDA:
1. Empowering Communities: In Year Two, 47 farmer groups were successfully established, engaging 3,500 individual farmers across four political districts in Nimba County. This initiative benefits approximately 8,160 households (average household size: 4). Impressively, over 65% of the farmers are women, emphasizing the project's dedication to gender inclusivity and women's empowerment.
2. Promoting Resilient Agricultural Practices: Farmers received support to multiply, and replant improved, climate-resilient seedlingssuch as enhanced rice seeds, cassava cuttings, and various vegetable seeds. This has led to increased productivity and incomes. Key accomplishments include:Distribution of equipment, safety gear, and tools for smoother farming operations. Establishment of 47 Farmer Field Schools (FFSs) in selected communities, offering on-farm training and capacity-building for low-carbon and sustainable farming techniques. Transition of eight business groups into fully registered entities, with two farmer groups forming functional cooperatives. Promotion of organic farming, with farmers producing and applying organic fertilizers to minimize chemical use.
3. Extension Support: Six extension officers were deployed to project communities to provide targeted assistance. Their contributions include hands-on support with plowing, soil leveling, nursery preparation, transplanting, composting, weed control, and rodent management.
4. Strengthening Market Linkages: The project facilitated market access for over 1,500 farmers by connecting them with potential buyers. Highlights include sales to wholesale buyers and local processors by 30 farmer groups, ensuring stable income streams; direct engagement with local markets by 14 groups, resulting in higher profit margins and stronger community presence.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
